correctness.rationale: Merca's Theorem 1.1 matches the coefficient convention and zero-extension of σ. Independently, the two-block series is half of the square of the single-block series minus its diagonal; Jacobi's two- and four-square identities and the diagonal coefficient σ(n/2)−4σ(n/4) give the same formula. In the normalized divisor sum the weights at 2-adic valuations 0,1,≥2 are 1,−1,3. Removing λ(n)/(4n) costs O_{h,ε}(X^{−1+ε}) by two divisor bounds of arbitrarily small exponent. The one-point factor at 2 is 1 and the odd factor is π²/8, before division by 4. For the pair, the CRT progression produces O(log²(X+h)/X) counting error; in the fixed-h tail, gcd(d,e)/(d²e²)≤h/(d²e²) even gives O_h(1/X). Grouping the local series by min(i,j), the odd factor is (p²+1)/(p²−1) times the truncated p^{−3} geometric sum. At 2 the successive increments are 1, −1/8 and 15·8^{−j} for j≥2, giving D(t). The odd baseline product is 3/2, hence the prefactor 3/32 after division by 16. Elementary bounds on π put π⁴/1024 strictly between 189/2000 (lag 5) and 7/72 (lag 3), and above 21/256 (lag 2); odd prime pair means decrease with p. Partial summation with weight n(n+1) gives X³/32+O_ε(X^{2+ε}) at lag 1. The fixed-h qualifications are essential to the stated review; RESULT.md lines 24–49 suffice to replay the argument.
